diagnosis: The baseline never grasps: code.py samples a grasp pose for the red cube, moves the end-effector to it, and then immediately executes the lift, place and open_gripper sequence without ever issuing close_gripper(). Every downstream primitive therefore acts on an empty gripper. This is why status-based triage is blind to it: all 9 primitives return [ok] on all three seeds and summary.txt reports FAILURES: 0, because each call individually succeeds at what it was asked to do — the causal chain breaks on an action that was never requested, not on one that errored. The keyframes confirm the whole chain is a no-op on the object: seed0_step003_goto_pose_after.png shows the open fingers correctly straddling the red cube at the sampled grasp pose (so perception, sample_grasp_pose and IK are all healthy), seed0_step004_goto_pose_after.png shows the arm at the +0.2 'post-pick' height with the red cube still flat on the table, and seed0_step008_goto_pose_after.png shows both cubes still side-by-side and unstacked at episode end. The red cube's pose is identical from reset to termination on every seed. Secondary observation from the same trace, fixed defensively rather than diagnostically: the green cube settles ~1cm after reset (z -0.087 at step 0 vs -0.09710775 when re-read at step 5), so any placement height computed from a pose read before the arm moves is stale; the baseline already re-reads green_pos at step 5 and is correct here, and fix_code.py preserves that ordering. IMPORTANT — outcome is 'fail', not 'success', because the repair is UNVALIDATED: the session sandbox is confined to the task directory, no runner exists inside it and the capx-path runner above it is unreachable, so zero replay attempts were possible against seeds 0/1/2. The diagnosis is high-confidence and evidence-backed; the repair is not tested. fix_code.py's close_gripper() call is inferred from the existence of open_gripper() and is not attested in code.py or trace.json — if that name is wrong the program raises NameError and regresses below baseline. See BLOCKED.md.

proposed_skills.name: all-ok-trace-with-unmoved-object-means-missing-actuation
proposed_skills.failure_signature: Every primitive returns [ok] and the summary reports FAILURES: 0, yet the task reward is zero and the target object's pose is unchanged between the first and last keyframe. Perception, grasp sampling and IK all look healthy in isolation.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Any manipulation task whose trace shows no failed primitive but no object motion either. Reach for this BEFORE re-tuning perception prompts, grasp poses or approach heights — a zero-failure trace actively misdirects toward those, because the primitives that did run all worked.
proposed_skills.strategy: Stop triaging by status and triage by causal chain instead: list the primitives the task requires, then diff that against the primitives the trace actually contains. A silent no-op episode is usually an omitted actuation primitive (close_gripper before transport, open_gripper before release, a missing lift), not a mis-parameterized one. Confirm by pairing the keyframe at the moment of the supposed state change (e.g. after the lift) against the object pose — if the arm is at height and the object is still on the table, the transport is carrying nothing. Prefer verifying the omission against an evidenced API name; a guessed primitive name turns a silent no-op into a hard NameError.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
# Trace shows: sample_grasp_pose -> goto_pose(grasp) -> goto_pose(lift) -> open_gripper
# Required chain:  sample_grasp_pose -> goto_pose(grasp) -> CLOSE -> goto_pose(lift) -> open_gripper
#                                                          ^^^^^ absent from trace, never errored
pick_pos, pick_quat = sample_grasp_pose(obj)
open_gripper()
goto_pose(pick_pos, pick_quat, z_approach=0.1)
close_gripper()          # the omitted link
lift = pick_pos.copy(); lift[2] += 0.2
goto_pose(lift, pick_quat)

proposed_skills.name: relocalize-target-after-scene-settle
proposed_skills.failure_signature: Object poses read immediately after reset disagree with the same object's pose re-read later in the episode by roughly a centimetre in z, with no contact in between (here: green cube z -0.087 at step 0 vs -0.09710775 at step 5). Placements computed from the early read land systematically high or low.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Any task that computes a placement, stacking or insertion height from a pose sampled before the arm has moved — stacking, put-in-container, put-on-shelf. Cheap to apply unconditionally.
proposed_skills.strategy: Objects are spawned marginally above their support at reset and settle once physics steps. Treat any pose read at t=0 as provisional. Re-read the SUPPORT object's pose immediately before computing the placement target, after the pick has already stepped the sim. Bounding-box extents are sizes rather than poses, so they are unaffected by settling and may safely be read once up front — only the position needs refreshing. Add a small release clearance on top of the computed contact height so the cube is dropped a few millimetres rather than driven into its support.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
# Extents are stable -> read once. Positions settle -> re-read late.
_, _, support_ext = get_object_pose(support, return_bbox_extent=True)
_, _, held_ext = get_object_pose(held, return_bbox_extent=True)
# ... pick and lift happen here, stepping the sim ...
support_pos, _, _ = get_object_pose(support, return_bbox_extent=False)  # settled
place = support_pos.copy()
place[2] = support_pos[2] + support_ext[2]/2 + held_ext[2]/2 + 0.005
goto_pose(place, pick_quat, z_approach=0.1)
open_gripper()
